evidence_items.publisher: Tow Center for Digital Journalism, Columbia Journalism Review
evidence_items.locator: Section: Chatbots’ responses to our queries were often confidently wrong

receipt.public_excerpt: incorrect answers to more than 60 percent of queries.

evidence_items.explanation: The study found substantial errors when eight search tools identified news articles from supplied excerpts. This supports concern about a specific consumer-facing task, but does not establish accuracy across ordinary questions or measure non-specialist expectations.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph reporting trust in accurate information; Methodology
evidence_items.explanation: The March survey shows divided trust rather than an uncomplicated expectation of accuracy. It is material caution against the broad expectation claim, but does not identify respondents' prompting expertise or directly test their expectations of particular answers.

unresolved_gaps: No matched study was recovered measuring both expectations and answer accuracy for users identified as non-specialists in prompting.
The retrieved accuracy evaluation covers article identification, not a representative distribution of everyday questions.
The speaker supplies no threshold at which an answer service becomes reliable.
